findings.source_passage: The Indian Sea breedeth the most and the biggest fishes that are: among which the Whales and Whirlpooles called Balaene, take up as much in length as four acres or arpens of land.
findings.why_it_matters: The Holland's Pliny extract contributes to the comic/encyclopedic range of sources Melville deliberately assembles; its archaic diction and absurd unit of measurement ('acres or arpens of land') are part of the tonal variety the Extracts establish.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Holland's Pliny extract in its original position among the early biblical/classical group.

findings.source_passage: Scarcely had we proceeded two days on the sea, when about sunrise a great many Whales and other monsters of the sea, appeared. Among the former, one was of a most monstrous size.... This came towards us, open-mouthed, raising the waves on all sides
findings.source_locator: early group, Tooke's Lucian / The True History
findings.why_it_matters: The Lucian extract is an early instance of the whale-as-monster-approaching-open-mouthed image, a motif central to the book's symbolic economy; its absence thins the mythological register of the early Extracts.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Tooke's Lucian extract in its original sequence position.

findings.source_passage: Let us fly, let us fly! Old Nick take me if it is not Leviathan described by the noble prophet Moses in the life of patient Job.
findings.why_it_matters: The Rabelais extract is tonally distinctive—comic, profane, and carnivalesque—and its contrast with the biblical solemnity around it is part of Melville's deliberate range-setting in the Extracts.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Rabelais extract in its original sequence position.

findings.source_passage: Which to secure, no skill of leach's art Mote him availle, but to returne againe To his wound's worker, that with lowly dart, Dinting his breast, had bred his restless paine, Like as the wounded whale to shore flies thro' the maine.
findings.why_it_matters: The Spenser extract is prosodically distinctive (archaic spelling, Spenserian register) and introduces the 'wounded whale' motif that resonates throughout the novel; its loss removes an important literary-historical layer.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore The Fairie Queen extract verbatim, preserving archaic spelling.

findings.source_passage: Spain—a great whale stranded on the shores of Europe.
findings.why_it_matters: This is among the most quotable single lines in the Extracts—Burke's metaphor extending whale-meaning into geopolitics—and the parenthetical '(somewhere)' is itself a signature Melvillean comic gesture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Burke 'Spain' extract and its attributed '(somewhere)' in full.

findings.source_passage: It is a matter of great astonishment that the consideration of the habits of so interesting, and, in a commercial point of view, so important an animal (as the Sperm Whale) should have been so entirely neglected
findings.source_locator: late group, Thomas Beale — second half of the extract
findings.why_it_matters: The Beale extract's second half—its aside on the astonishing neglect of the Sperm Whale's habits—carries interpretive weight as a meta-commentary on the book's own project; cutting it leaves only the action description and loses the reflective dimension.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full Beale extract including the 'matter of great astonishment' passage.

findings.source_passage: In the free element beneath me swam, Floundered and dived, in play, in chace, in battle, Fishes of every colour, form, and kind; Which language cannot paint
findings.source_locator: middle group, Montgomery's World before the Flood
findings.why_it_matters: The Montgomery verse is a sustained poetic extract that broadens the register; its 'which language cannot paint' phrase anticipates Melville's own claims about the whale's ineffability.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider restoring the Montgomery extract if word budget permits.

findings.why_it_matters: The Cooper extract introduces vernacular sailor speech and the Right Whale / Sperm Whale distinction early, both recurring concerns in the novel.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Cooper's Pilot extract if budget allows.

summary: The draft preserves most of the highest-profile extracts verbatim but silently drops a significant number of mid-sequence entries—Rabelais, Spenser, Burke ('Spain'), Holland's Pliny, Tooke's Lucian, Montgomery, Cooper, and truncates Beale—producing five medium-severity losses that together trigger regeneration.
